The Chapter House, Westminster Abbey, London

The Pyx Chamber was built in the years immediately after the Norman Conquest, and is one of the oldest parts of Westminster Abbey. It originally formed part of an undercroft below the monks' dormitory.

For much of the Middle Ages and afterwards, the Pyx Chamber served as a strong-room, containing valuables left there by the king. The thick walls, double doors (with 6 locks) and iron window-bars were intended as a safeguard against burglary, particularly after a nearby treasury was robbed in 1303.

The name 'Pyx' refers to small boxes, containing the official samples of gold and silver coinage which were also kept here. New coins were annually tested against these samples in a public 'Trial of the Pyx', held in the Palace of Westminster.

The Chapter House and Pyx Chamber are jointly managed by the Dean and Chapter of Westminster and English Heritage., Westminster Abbey, London
